reason: Hardware limitation: CPU-only inference with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct is impractically slow for the required 40 episodes (N=10 × 4 conditions).

details.bottleneck_identified: First LLM inference call takes approximately 176 seconds (cold start + PyTorch JIT compilation). Subsequent calls stabilize at ~3s each on CPU. However, with 4-8 candidates per step and 3 ensemble checkpoints, each step requires 12-24 model inference calls, making a single episode take 10-60+ minutes.

attempted_approaches.approach: Sandbox v2 (Docker peda-sandbox:v2) with partial adapter
attempted_approaches.result: First inference never completed within 600s timeout. Sandbox prompt requires JSON state+file prediction (~80+ output tokens), compounding latency.

attempted_approaches.approach: Grid World with partial adapter + 3 ensemble checkpoints
attempted_approaches.result: Each ensemble checkpoint load/unload via PEFT takes ~10-30s on CPU. 3 checkpoints × 4 candidates = 12 adapter loads per step. First episode did not complete within 600s.

attempted_approaches.approach: Grid World with empty ensemble (model confidence-based epistemic signal)
attempted_approaches.result: Fastest approach (no adapter switching). Model loaded in 2.5s. First inference still takes ~176s cold start. The first episode (PEDA + Pragmatic, ~6 inference calls each) did not complete within 780s wall time.

pilot_results_reference.note: Pilot N=1 shows directional signal but insufficient for statistical inference. Required N>=10 per condition.

recommendation: Phase 3 confirmatory experiment requires GPU acceleration (any CUDA-capable GPU would provide 10-50x speedup over CPU). With GPU, estimated runtime for 40 episodes: 10-30 minutes. Without GPU, the experiment is impractical (estimated 60-120 hours total on this CPU).
script_available: scripts/phase3_fast.py (Grid World, no ensemble, model confidence-based epistemic)
